rules.title: Explicitly enable or disable tests parallelization
rules.description: By default, MSTest runs tests within the same assembly sequentially, which can lead to severe performance limitations. It is recommended to enable assembly attribute '[Parallelize]' to run tests in parallel, or if the assembly is known to not be parallelizable, to use explicitly the assembly level attribute '[DoNotParallelize]'.

rules.title: Test classes should have valid layout
rules.description:
Test classes, classes marked with the '[TestClass]' attribute, should respect the following layout to be considered valid by MSTest:
- it should be 'public' (or 'internal' if '[assembly: DiscoverInternals]' attribute is set)
- it should not be 'static' (except if it contains only 'AssemblyInitialize' and/or 'AssemblyCleanup' methods)
- it should not be generic.

rules.title: Test methods should have valid layout
rules.description:
Test methods, methods marked with the '[TestMethod]' attribute, should respect the following layout to be considered valid by MSTest:
- it should be 'public' (or 'internal' if '[assembly: DiscoverInternals]' attribute is set)
- it should not be 'static'
- it should may be generic as long as type parameters can be inferred and argument types are compatible
- it should not be 'abstract'
- return type should be 'void', 'Task' or 'ValueTask'
- it should not be 'async void'
- it should not be a special method (finalizer, operator...).

rules.title: Public types should be test classes
rules.description: It's considered a good practice to have only test classes marked public in a test project.

rules.title: Test context property should have valid layout
rules.description:
'TestContext' should be a non-static property assigned in constructor or set by MSTest. To be set by MSTest, it should follow the layout:
- it should be 'public' regardless of whether '[assembly: DiscoverInternals]' attribute is set or not.
- it should not be 'static'
- it should have a setter.

rules.title: [Owner] can only be set on methods marked with [TestMethod]
rules.description: MSTest ignores these attributes outside a test context.

rules.title: TestInitialize method should have valid layout
rules.description:
Methods marked with '[TestInitialize]' should follow the following layout to be valid:
-it should be 'public'
-it should not be 'abstract'
-it should not be 'async void'
-it should not be 'static'
-it should not be a special method (finalizer, operator...).
-it should not be generic
-it should not take any parameter
-return type should be 'void', 'Task' or 'ValueTask'

The type declaring these methods should also respect the following rules:
-The type should be a class
-The class should be 'public' or 'internal' (if the test project is using the '[DiscoverInternals]' attribute)
-The class shouldn't be 'static'
-If the class is 'sealed', it should be marked with '[TestClass]' (or a derived attribute).

rules.title: TestCleanup method should have valid layout
rules.description:
Methods marked with '[TestCleanup]' should follow the following layout to be valid:
-it should be 'public'
-it should not be 'abstract'
-it should not be 'async void'
-it should not be 'static'
-it should not be a special method (finalizer, operator...).
-it should not be generic
-it should not take any parameter
-return type should be 'void', 'Task' or 'ValueTask'

The type declaring these methods should also respect the following rules:
-The type should be a class
-The class should be 'public' or 'internal' (if the test project is using the '[DiscoverInternals]' attribute)
-The class shouldn't be 'static'
-If the class is 'sealed', it should be marked with '[TestClass]' (or a derived attribute).

rules.title: ClassInitialize methods should have valid layout
rules.description:
Methods marked with '[ClassInitialize]' should follow the following layout to be valid:
-it can't be declared on a generic class without the 'InheritanceBehavior' mode is set
-it should be 'public'
-it should be 'static'
-it should not be 'async void'
-it should not be a special method (finalizer, operator...).
-it should not be generic
-it should take one parameter of type 'TestContext'
-return type should be 'void', 'Task' or 'ValueTask'
-'InheritanceBehavior.BeforeEachDerivedClass' attribute parameter should be specified if the class is 'abstract'
-'InheritanceBehavior.BeforeEachDerivedClass' attribute parameter should not be specified if the class is 'sealed'

The type declaring these methods should also respect the following rules:
-The type should be a class
-The class should be 'public' or 'internal' (if the test project is using the '[DiscoverInternals]' attribute)
-The class shouldn't be 'static'
-If the class is 'sealed', it should be marked with '[TestClass]' (or a derived attribute)
-the class should not be generic.

rules.title: ClassCleanup methods should have valid layout
rules.description:
Methods marked with '[ClassCleanup]' should follow the following layout to be valid:
-it can't be declared on a generic class without the 'InheritanceBehavior' mode is set
-it should be 'public'
-it should be 'static'
-it should not be 'async void'
-it should not be a special method (finalizer, operator...).
-it should not be generic
-it should either not take any parameter, or take a single parameter of type 'TestContext'
-return type should be 'void', 'Task' or 'ValueTask'
-'InheritanceBehavior.BeforeEachDerivedClass' attribute parameter should be specified if the class is 'abstract'
-'InheritanceBehavior.BeforeEachDerivedClass' attribute parameter should not be specified if the class is 'sealed'

The type declaring these methods should also respect the following rules:
-The type should be a class
-The class should be 'public' or 'internal' (if the test project is using the '[DiscoverInternals]' attribute)
-The class shouldn't be 'static'
-If the class is 'sealed', it should be marked with '[TestClass]' (or a derived attribute)
-the class should not be generic.

rules.title: AssemblyInitialize methods should have valid layout
rules.description:
Methods marked with '[AssemblyInitialize]' should follow the following layout to be valid:
-it can't be declared on a generic class
-it should be 'public'
-it should be 'static'
-it should not be 'async void'
-it should not be a special method (finalizer, operator...).
-it should not be generic
-it should take one parameter of type 'TestContext'
-return type should be 'void', 'Task' or 'ValueTask'

The type declaring these methods should also respect the following rules:
-The type should be a class
-The class should be 'public' or 'internal' (if the test project is using the '[DiscoverInternals]' attribute)
-The class shouldn't be 'static'
-The class should be marked with '[TestClass]' (or a derived attribute)
-the class should not be generic.

rules.title: AssemblyCleanup methods should have valid layout
rules.description:
Methods marked with '[AssemblyCleanup]' should follow the following layout to be valid:
-it can't be declared on a generic class
-it should be 'public'
-it should be 'static'
-it should not be 'async void'
-it should not be a special method (finalizer, operator...).
-it should not be generic
-it should either not take any parameter, or take a single parameter of type 'TestContext'
-return type should be 'void', 'Task' or 'ValueTask'

The type declaring these methods should also respect the following rules:
-The type should be a class
-The class should be 'public' or 'internal' (if the test project is using the '[DiscoverInternals]' attribute)
-The class shouldn't be 'static'
-The class should be marked with '[TestClass]' (or a derived attribute)
-the class should not be generic.

rules.title: DataRow should be valid
Test method should not be ignored
rules.description: Test methods should not be ignored (marked with '[Ignore]').

rules.title: Test class should have test method
rules.description: Test class should have at least one test method or be 'static' with method(s) marked by '[AssemblyInitialize]' and/or '[AssemblyCleanup]'.

rules.title: Assertion arguments should be passed in the correct order
rules.description: 'Assert.AreEqual', 'Assert.AreNotEqual', 'Assert.AreSame' and 'Assert.AreNotSame' expects the expected value to be passed first and the actual value to be passed as second argument.

rules.title: DynamicData should be valid
Prefer TestInitialize methods over constructors
rules.description: '[TestInitialize]' supports both synchronous and asynchronous initialization, whereas constructors cannot be awaited. This opt-in style rule is mutually exclusive with MSTEST0020.

rules.title: Prefer constructors over TestInitialize methods
rules.description: Constructors allow initialization through 'readonly' fields and provide stronger compiler feedback, especially with nullable reference types. This opt-in style rule is mutually exclusive with MSTEST0019.

rules.title: Prefer 'Dispose' over TestCleanup methods
rules.description: 'Dispose' and 'DisposeAsync' follow standard .NET lifetime patterns, making test cleanup consistent with production code. This opt-in style rule is mutually exclusive with MSTEST0022.

rules.title: Prefer TestCleanup over 'Dispose' methods
rules.description: '[TestCleanup]' supports asynchronous cleanup on target frameworks where 'IAsyncDisposable' is unavailable. This opt-in style rule is mutually exclusive with MSTEST0021.

rules.title: Do not negate boolean assertions
rules.description: Using the opposite assertion directly makes the test easier to read and produces clearer failure diagnostics.

rules.title: Do not store TestContext in a static member
rules.description: The TestContext passed to assembly or class initialization is specific to that context and is not updated for each test execution. Reusing it in a 'static' member can expose stale context.

rules.title: Use 'Assert.Fail' instead of an always-failing assert
rules.description: 'Assert.Fail' makes an intentional failure explicit and allows the failure message to document why the test cannot continue.

rules.title: Avoid conditional access in assertions
rules.description: Conditional access adds an implicit null branch to an assertion, which can hide whether the object was unexpectedly null. A separate null assertion makes failures identify the violated condition.

rules.title: Public methods should be test methods
rules.description: Public methods should be test methods (marked with `[TestMethod]`).

rules.title: Type containing '[TestMethod]' should be marked with '[TestClass]'
rules.description: Type containing '[TestMethod]' should be marked with '[TestClass]', otherwise the test method will be silently ignored.

rules.title: 'System.ComponentModel.DescriptionAttribute' has no effect on test methods
rules.description: 'System.ComponentModel.DescriptionAttribute' has no effect in the context of tests and you likely wanted to use 'Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting.DescriptionAttribute' instead.

rules.title: Assertion condition is always true
rules.description: An assertion that can never fail does not verify behavior and obscures the condition the test is intended to check.

rules.title: '[DeploymentItem]' can be specified only on test class or test method
rules.description: MSTest ignores '[DeploymentItem]' when it is applied outside a test class or test method.

rules.title: Do not use shadowing
rules.description: Shadowing test members could cause testing issues (such as NRE).

rules.title: Use proper 'Assert' methods
rules.description: Specialized assertion methods improve readability and provide more precise failure diagnostics.

rules.title: Don't use 'Assert.AreSame' or 'Assert.AreNotSame' with value types
rules.description: Use 'Assert.AreEqual'/'Assert.AreNotEqual' instead of 'Assert.AreSame'/'Assert.AreNotSame' when comparing value types. Passing a value type to 'Assert.AreSame'/'Assert.AreNotSame' will be boxed (creating a new object). Because 'Assert.AreSame'/'Assert.AreNotSame' does the comparison by reference, 'Assert.AreSame' will fail when boxing happens, and 'Assert.AreNotSame' will always pass.

rules.title: Do not assert inside 'async void' contexts
rules.description: Do not assert inside 'async void' methods, local functions, or lambdas. Exceptions that are thrown in this context will be unhandled exceptions. When using VSTest under .NET Framework, they will be silently swallowed. When using Microsoft.Testing.Platform or VSTest under modern .NET, they may crash the process.

rules.title: Use 'ConditionBaseAttribute' on test classes
rules.description: When applied to a class, MSTest evaluates condition attributes only if the class is a test class, so applying them to a non-test class has no effect.

rules.title: Avoid duplicated 'DataRow' entries
Use retry attribute on test method or test class
rules.description: Retry attributes have no effect on methods or classes that MSTest does not recognize as tests.

rules.title: Prefer 'TestMethod' over 'DataTestMethod'
rules.description: 'DataTestMethodAttribute' is obsolete and provides no additional functionality over 'TestMethodAttribute'. Use 'TestMethodAttribute' for all test methods, including parameterized tests.

rules.title: Use 'CooperativeCancellation = true' with '[Timeout]'
rules.description: Using '[Timeout]' without explicitly setting 'CooperativeCancellation = true' is discouraged. In a future version, cooperative cancellation will become the default behavior. Set 'CooperativeCancellation = true' to opt into the recommended behavior and avoid breaking changes.

rules.title: Use 'Assert' instead of 'StringAssert'
rules.description: 'StringAssert' methods have equivalent 'Assert' counterparts. Using one assertion API improves consistency and discoverability.

rules.title: TestContext property cannot be accessed in this context
rules.description: Some TestContext properties are only available during test execution and cannot be accessed in assembly initialize, class initialize, class cleanup, or assembly cleanup methods.

rules.title: Flow TestContext.CancellationToken to async operations
rules.description: When calling async methods that have overloads accepting a CancellationToken parameter, prefer using the overload with TestContext.CancellationToken to enable cooperative cancellation and respect test timeouts.

rules.title: GlobalTestInitialize and GlobalTestCleanup methods should have valid layout
rules.description:
Methods marked with '[GlobalTestInitialize]' or '[GlobalTestCleanup]' should follow the following layout to be valid:
-it can't be declared on a generic class
-it should be 'public'
-it should be 'static'
-it should not be 'async void'
-it should not be a special method (finalizer, operator...).
-it should not be generic
-it should take one parameter of type 'TestContext'
-return type should be 'void', 'Task' or 'ValueTask'

The type declaring these methods should also respect the following rules:
-The type should be a class
-The class should be 'public'
-The class should be marked with '[TestClass]' (or a derived attribute)
-the class should not be generic.

rules.title: Assert.Throws should contain only a single statement/expression
rules.description: Assert.Throws methods should contain only a single statement or expression. Multiple statements can be misleading - if the first statement throws, subsequent statements are never executed; if it doesn't throw, it should be moved outside the Assert.Throws.

rules.title: Avoid passing an explicit 'DynamicDataSourceType' and use the default auto detect behavior
rules.description: Since MSTest 3.8, 'DynamicDataSourceType.AutoDetect' is the default and automatically identifies properties, methods, and fields, reducing verbosity and coupling to the member kind.

rules.title: Use TestContext.CancellationToken instead of TestContext.CancellationTokenSource.Token
rules.description: TestContext.CancellationToken provides a more direct way to access the cancellation token compared to TestContext.CancellationTokenSource.Token.

rules.title: Do not ignore the return value of string methods
rules.description: Methods like Contains, StartsWith, and EndsWith return boolean values that indicate whether the condition was met. Ignoring these return values is likely a mistake.

rules.title: TestMethodAttribute should set DisplayName correctly
rules.description: In MSTest 4 and later, the string constructor argument represents the caller file path rather than the test display name.

rules.title: TestMethodAttribute derived class should propagate source information
rules.description: Propagating the source file and line number allows MSTest to report accurate diagnostics, test results, and Test Explorer navigation.

rules.title: Do not use asserts in catch blocks
rules.description: Using asserts in catch blocks is problematic because the test will pass even if no exception is thrown and the catch block is never executed. Use 'Assert.Throws', 'Assert.ThrowsExactly', 'Assert.ThrowsAsync' or 'Assert.ThrowsExactlyAsync' to verify that an exception is thrown, and then make additional assertions on the caught exception without using the try-catch block. The rule also flags 'throw new AssertFailedException(...)' and 'throw new AssertInconclusiveException(...)' (the desugared forms of 'Assert.Fail' and 'Assert.Inconclusive'). 'Assert.Inconclusive' (and 'throw new AssertInconclusiveException(...)') is exempt when used inside a filtered catch ('catch (...) when (...)'), because demoting a caught failure to an Inconclusive outcome is the only use case that cannot be expressed without a catch block. For other intentional bypasses (for example, attaching a runtime-built message to the failure), suppress the diagnostic with '#pragma warning disable MSTEST0058'.

rules.title: Do not use both '[Parallelize]' and '[DoNotParallelize]' attributes
rules.description: An assembly should have either '[Parallelize]' or '[DoNotParallelize]' attribute, but not both. Having both attributes creates an ambiguous configuration. When both are present, '[DoNotParallelize]' takes precedence and parallelization will be disabled.

rules.title: Avoid duplicate test method attributes
rules.description: A test method should be marked with exactly one attribute that is or inherits from 'TestMethodAttribute'. When multiple such attributes are present, only the first one returned by reflection will be used.

rules.title: Use '[OSCondition]' attribute instead of 'RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform' calls with early return or 'Assert.Inconclusive'
rules.description: Test methods that use 'RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform' with early return or 'Assert.Inconclusive' should use the '[OSCondition]' attribute instead. This attribute provides a more declarative and discoverable way to specify OS-specific test requirements.

rules.title: Avoid using 'out' or 'ref' parameters in test methods
rules.description: 'out' and 'ref' parameters add no value in test methods and they can safely be replaced by normal parameters.

rules.title: Test classes should have valid constructors
rules.description: Test classes must have a public constructor that is either parameterless or accepts a single TestContext parameter. This allows the test framework to instantiate the test class properly.

rules.title: Prefer async assertion methods
rules.description: When verifying exceptions from asynchronous code, use the async assertion methods instead of blocking the asynchronous operation with GetAwaiter().GetResult().

rules.title: Avoid Assert.AreEqual on collection types
rules.description: `Assert.AreEqual` and `Assert.AreNotEqual` use `EqualityComparer<T>.Default`. For collection-like types this relies on the type's own equality semantics instead of comparing sequence elements, so `Assert.AreSequenceEqual`/`Assert.AreNotSequenceEqual` or `Assert.AreEquivalent`/`Assert.AreNotEquivalent` are usually the better fit.

rules.title: '[Ignore]' should specify a justification
rules.description: An '[Ignore]' attribute applied to a test method or test class should include a non-empty message explaining why the test or class is ignored. A justification message makes it easier to triage skipped tests, helps reviewers understand the intent, and prevents tests from being silently disabled forever.

rules.title: Avoid synchronously blocking calls such as 'Thread.Sleep', 'Task.Wait', 'Task.WaitAll', 'Task.WaitAny' or 'Task<TResult>.Result' in test code
rules.description: Synchronously blocking the current thread with 'Thread.Sleep', 'Task.Wait', 'Task.WaitAll', 'Task.WaitAny' or 'Task<TResult>.Result' inside test methods or test fixtures is a common source of flakiness and can also deadlock when the test framework runs tests on a SynchronizationContext that requires cooperative scheduling. Prefer 'await Task.Delay' for time-based waits and 'await' the task to observe its result.

rules.title: Use 'Assert' instead of 'CollectionAssert'
rules.description: 'CollectionAssert' methods have equivalent 'Assert' counterparts. Using one assertion API improves consistency and discoverability.

rules.title: '[MemberCondition]' arguments should be valid
rules.description: The members referenced by a '[MemberCondition]' attribute must exist on the referenced type, be 'public static', return 'bool', and (for methods) be parameterless. The attribute throws at runtime when these rules are violated; this analyzer surfaces the same problems at build time so typos and refactors do not silently break test gating.

rules.title: Test method should not specify a display name equal to its name
rules.description: Setting a 'DisplayName' on a test method to a value that is identical to the method name is redundant because the method name is already used as the display name by default. The redundant 'DisplayName' can be removed without changing how the test is reported.

rules.title: '[AssemblyFixtureProvider]' is not supported with ahead-of-time compilation
rules.description: '[AssemblyFixtureProvider]' discovery relies on walking the runtime assembly reference graph, which is not supported when the runtime cannot generate dynamic code (for example under Native AOT or Blazor WebAssembly AOT). The attribute is ignored in such builds, so the provided assembly initialize and cleanup methods will not run. Declare the '[AssemblyInitialize]' and '[AssemblyCleanup]' methods directly in the test assembly instead.

rules.title: Prefer a named constant for the '[ResourceLock]' resource key
rules.description: '[ResourceLock]' matches tests by exact string equality of the resource key. A bare string literal fails open: a typo produces a different key, so conflicting tests are no longer serialized and race silently instead of failing with an error. Referencing a shared constant makes typos a compile error and lets the compiler enforce that every test contending on the same resource uses the same key.

rules.title: Test mutating process-global state should declare a resource lock
rules.description: Mutating process-global state (such as environment variables or the console redirection) from a test is unsafe once in-assembly parallelization is enabled, because a sibling test running concurrently observes the mutation. Unlike '[ResourceLock]', which fails open when a key is forgotten, this rule flags the mutation at compile time. Declare '[ResourceLock]' with the matching 'WellKnownResources' key to serialize contending tests, or '[DoNotParallelize]' to opt the test out of parallelization.

rules.title: Avoid changing the current directory in a parallelized test
rules.description: The current directory is process-global on every operating system and, unlike culture, has no thread-scoped or async-scoped equivalent. A test that changes it corrupts the working directory of every test running concurrently, and relative paths resolved elsewhere in the suite silently point at the wrong location. A '[ResourceLock]' serializes the contending tests and makes the mutation safe, but it remains a design smell in a parallel suite: prefer passing absolute paths so the current directory never needs to change.

rules.title: Avoid mutating process-wide culture in a parallelized test
rules.description: 'CultureInfo.DefaultThreadCurrentCulture' and 'DefaultThreadCurrentUICulture' set the default culture for the whole process, so every concurrently running test observes the change and formatting or parsing can be corrupted under in-assembly parallelization. The per-thread and ambient forms are intentionally not flagged: on modern .NET the 'Thread.CurrentThread.CurrentCulture' / 'CurrentUICulture' and 'CultureInfo.CurrentCulture' / 'CurrentUICulture' setters all assign an 'AsyncLocal'-backed value that flows with the execution context, so they do not corrupt sibling tests or leak onto later-pooled threads. Because the flagged setters are process-wide, restoring the previous value in a 'finally' does not help - concurrently running tests still observe the changed culture for the duration of the mutation; declare '[DoNotParallelize]' on the test, or avoid mutating process-wide culture, instead.

rules.title: Avoid hardcoded or shared filesystem paths in a parallelized test
rules.description: Passing a hardcoded absolute path, or a relative path literal, directly to a filesystem-mutating 'File.*'/'Directory.*' method (for example 'File.WriteAllText' or 'Directory.CreateDirectory') targets a location shared by every other test in the assembly; relative paths additionally resolve against the process-global current directory. Under in-assembly parallelization two tests can then write to the same location concurrently. Only statically constant paths passed to a mutating API are flagged; reads, path construction, and paths built from variables are left to the parallel-safety audit skill. Prefer a unique per-test directory such as 'TestContext.TestTempDirectory'.

rules.title: '[DependsOn]' arguments should be valid
rules.description: A '[DependsOn]' attribute references a test by name. A reference that matches no test is deliberately non-fatal at run time, so that running a subset of the suite stays possible, which means a typo or a rename silently drops the declared ordering. This analyzer reports the problems that can be decided at build time: a method that does not exist on the referenced type, a target that is not a test, a test that depends on itself, a dependency cycle visible in the compilation, a reference to a type from another assembly (dependencies are resolved within a single test source), and an attribute applied where it has no effect.

rules.title: Use '[ArchitectureCondition]' attribute instead of 'RuntimeInformation.ProcessArchitecture' checks with early return or 'Assert.Inconclusive'
rules.description: Test methods that compare 'RuntimeInformation.ProcessArchitecture' and then early return or call 'Assert.Inconclusive' should use the '[ArchitectureCondition]' attribute instead. This attribute provides a more declarative and discoverable way to specify architecture-specific test requirements, and it reports the test as skipped rather than passed, which an early return does not.

rules.title: Use '[CICondition]' attribute instead of 'Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable' checks with early return or 'Assert.Inconclusive'
rules.description: Test methods that null-check the 'CI' environment variable and then early return or call 'Assert.Inconclusive' should use the '[CICondition]' attribute instead. This attribute recognizes all the continuous integration providers MSTest knows about and parses their values, and it reports the test as skipped rather than passed, which an early return does not.

rules.title: '[TestFilterProvider]' should reference a valid test filter type
rules.description: '[assembly: TestFilterProvider(typeof(MyFilter))]' passes the filter type as a 'Type', so the compiler accepts any type at all. The adapter validates it only when it materializes the filter, and then fails the whole run. The referenced type must be non-generic and instantiable, implement 'ITestFilter' and expose a public parameterless constructor, and at most one provider may be registered per test assembly. When targeting .NET, the generic '[assembly: TestFilterProvider<MyFilter>]' form enforces the interface and constructor requirements through generic constraints instead.

rules.title: A test class inherits a lifecycle or test method from a different MSTest version
rules.description: MSTest resolves the inherited lifecycle attributes '[TestInitialize]', '[TestCleanup]', '[ClassInitialize]' and '[ClassCleanup]', and the test attributes '[TestMethod]' and '[DataTestMethod]', by their exact framework type identity. The framework assembly was renamed from 'Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestPlatform.TestFramework' to 'MSTest.TestFramework', so a base class compiled against a different MSTest major exposes these attributes with a different type identity. When such a base is inherited by a test class compiled against another version, the inherited setup and cleanup do not run and inherited test methods are not discovered, with no build error and no discovery error. Recompile the base assembly and, for custom attributes, the assembly that defines the attribute against the same MSTest version as the test project.

rules.title: Use '[ExecutableCondition]' attribute instead of 'File.Exists' checks before 'Process.Start'
rules.description: Test methods that use 'File.Exists' to skip a test before starting the same executable with 'Process.Start' should use the '[ExecutableCondition]' attribute instead. This attribute provides a declarative and discoverable tool requirement and reports an early return as a skipped test rather than a passed test.

rules.title: Platform compatibility attributes should be consistent with '[OSCondition]'
rules.description: 'SupportedOSPlatformAttribute' and 'UnsupportedOSPlatformAttribute' inform platform compatibility analysis but do not control MSTest execution. Test methods and test classes that use these attributes should also declare a compatible '[OSCondition]' so tests are skipped on unsupported operating-system families at run time. '[OSCondition]' does not enforce platform version constraints.

rules.title: '[TestClass]' should not be applied to abstract classes
rules.description: MSTest ignores '[TestClass]' attributes applied to abstract classes. Test methods declared by an abstract class are discovered through concrete derived test classes, which must declare their own '[TestClass]' attribute.

rules.title: Remove redundant test method attribute
rules.description: A method-level attribute should be removed when the containing test class already establishes equivalent or more restrictive behavior.

rules.title: Avoid duplicated 'DataRow' display names
rules.description: Duplicate 'DataRow' display names make data-driven test cases indistinguishable in test results and test explorers.

rules.title: MSTest host test-class injection is not supported by the selected build mode
rules.description: Host-owned MSTest test-class injection uses reflection-based Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection activation. Remove AddMSTestTestClassInjection or disable the unsupported build mode.

rules.title: Do not combine 'DisplayName' and 'ArgumentsDisplayName'
rules.description: Specify either 'DisplayName' for a full test case name or 'ArgumentsDisplayName' for an argument label that retains the method display name, but not both. Remove the ignored 'ArgumentsDisplayName' to preserve the current name, or remove 'DisplayName' to use the argument label.
